page: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The host system is driven by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 10 dedicated physical cores and 20 vCPUs across two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AMX (tile and int8), alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration through AES and VAES.

System memory totals 160.0 GB, yielding a high 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly via 1,181 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, supplemented by Premium Storage support. The instance does not include discrete GPUs (0.0 count). Memory subsystem testing records 150.84 GB/sec of uncached large-block read throughput and 78.61 GB/sec of uncached write throughput, alongside a small-block cached read speed of 1,565.06 GB/sec.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution across most general workloads, highlighted by an average Geekbench multi-core score of 11,504.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 32,372.66. Compute and compression metrics show particular strength in single-threaded gzip compression at 31.28 GB/sec (top 25%) and lightweight LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model reaching 393.88 tokens/sec (top 10%). Standard in-memory data tests register 28.38 million operations/sec for Redis SET transactions and a PassMark database score of 11,736.32.

With its 160.0 GB memory footprint paired with 1,181 GB NVMe local scratch storage, the E20ds_v6 delivers solid density for memory-bound tasks without requiring high-core licensing allocations. The instance fits in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, medium-scale data processing pipelines, and localized search indexing engines.
